targetWords.definition: If someone is bankrupt, then they are unable to pay their debts.
targetWords.example: The store had few customers and soon went bankrupt.

targetWords.definition: To conform to rules or laws is to obey them.
targetWords.example: The new student had to conform to the school's dress code.

targetWords.definition: To employ someone means to give work to them.
targetWords.example: The bookstore employed two full-time clerks.

targetWords.definition: To expel someone means to force them to leave a place.
targetWords.example: Since he would not follow the rules, the principal had to expel the student.

targetWords.definition: An extension is a part added to something to give it more time or space.
targetWords.example: My parents decided to add an extension to our house for the new baby.

targetWords.definition: If something is forthcoming, then it is about to happen in the future.
targetWords.example: ■ Some economists predicted that the forthcoming world economy would be severe.

targetWords.definition: To furnish means to put furniture in a house or room.
targetWords.example: Most homes are furnished with tables, chairs, and beds.

targetWords.definition: Hygiene is the conditions or methods needed for health and cleanliness.
targetWords.example: People who brush their teeth at least twice a day are practicing good hygiene.

targetWords.definition: If something is hygienic, then it is clean and unlikely to cause disease. - » My sister works very hard to keep her entire home as hygienic as possible. landlord [laenc/loird] n.
—► The landlord collected everyone's rent money on the first day of every month.
targetWords.example: The landlord collected everyone's rent money on the first day of every month. Ca 63

targetWords.definition: To lease means to rent property, usually an apartment or land.
targetWords.example: When the family first leased the apartment, the rent was very low.

targetWords.definition: If something is mandatory, then it is required by law.
targetWords.example: It's mandatory that everyone be at least sixteen to drive a car in the US.

targetWords.definition: To mend something means to fix it when it is broken or damaged.
targetWords.example: Mother mended the rip in my pants with a piece of cloth. mortgage [md:rgid3 ] n.

targetWords.definition: —► When they bought their new home, the married couple had to sign a mortgage.
targetWords.example: When they bought their new home, the married couple had to sign a mortgage.

targetWords.definition: Personnel are employees in a business.
targetWords.example: When business increased, we had to hire more personnel.

targetWords.definition: Plumbing is the system of pipes used in a home to supply water.
targetWords.example: When the plumbing stopped working, no one was allowed to use the toilets. tenant [tenant] n.

targetWords.definition: -» The new tenants moved into the house across the street.
targetWords.example: The new tenants moved into the house across the street.

targetWords.definition: If something is trendy, then it is very popular and new.
targetWords.example: Carlo bought a trendy new car. utility [ju:tflati] n.

targetWords.definition: —► If you don't pay the utilities, you may have your electricity turned off.
targetWords.example: If you don't pay the utilities, you may have your electricity turned off.

targetWords.definition: Whereby means by which or through which.
targetWords.example: The mayor had a new bridge built whereby the citizens could cross the river.
